traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 32 records annotated as flowering (Feb 1, Mar 4, Apr 19, May 5, Jun 1, Jul 1, Aug 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, March to May. FEIS (Vaccinium parvifolium) gives April to June for the Northwest.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 41 plant-years at 17 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Feb 4, Jun 9, Jul 20, Aug 21, Sep 11, Oct 7, Nov 2); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, June to October. FEIS (Vaccinium parvifolium): ripe from July to September in British Columbia, Oregon and Washington.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Vaccinium parvifolium: grows 1 m to 4 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Vaccinium parvifolium: leaves 8 mm to 3.5 cm long.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an airy shrub of bright green, angled twigs with small, thin, rounded leaves and translucent red berries; it often grows from old stumps and logs. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 2.5 m tall at 15 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green twigs and leaves; red berries. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: single red berries about 1 cm across, crowned by the calyx, a quarter still pale. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: greenish-pink bells in April and May; berries red from late June into August. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of North America (vol. 8) on Vaccinium parvifolium, through JSTOR Global Plants, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): corolla globose to urceolate, 4 to 6 by 3 to 5 mm, pink, bronze or yellowish green; calyx lobes spreading, broadly ovate, 0.4 to 0.6 mm. Its genus account: ovary inferior, 4- or 5-locular; stamens 8 to 10.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): an urn on an inferior ovary from the characters by the rules at the flowering plants. Five petals and five tiny calyx lobes by hand, as the Flora of North America has them, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read); it gives no count.
